walkthroughs.body_html:
Textiles — a core area of GCSE Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Textiles brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Textiles.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In weaving, the threads held under tension running lengthwise on the loom are the:
options: Selvedge
Warp
Weft
Bias
Printing with a carved lino block.
Using wax to resist dye in chosen areas.
Stitching shapes onto a background.
Matting fibres with soap and friction.
Weaving threads on a loom.
Burning designs into fabric.
Stitching cut fabric shapes onto a base fabric.
Dyeing folded and tied cloth.
Matting wool fibres with warm water, soap and friction.
Knitting wool with needles.
Gluing threads onto paper.
Spinning fibres into yarn only.
Yes — all fabric is made by weaving threads.
No — felt is non-woven; loose fibres are matted together with moisture and friction.
It stiffens the fabric ready for embroidery.
Yes — felt is knitted from thick yarn.

mcqs.q: In batik, what does the wax do?
options: Yes — felt is knitted from thick yarn.
It stiffens the fabric ready for embroidery.
It resists the dye, so waxed areas keep their original colour.
The wax is the dye and adds the colour.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between warp and weft?
options: Warp threads run lengthwise under tension; the weft is woven across, over and under them.
Warp and weft are two names for the same threads.
Yes — felt is knitted from thick yarn.
Warp is the colour and weft is the texture.

sequence.term: Lay out the wool fibres in layers
sequence.def: Felt begins with crossed layers of loose fibre
Moisture and soap prepare the fibres to bond

sequence.term: Rub and roll to felt the fibres
sequence.def: Agitation locks the fibres into fabric
Soap is washed out once the felt holds
The damp fabric is formed and left to dry
Decoration is added to the finished felt
